input: A tool coverage recount ran 25 tools on 10 sealed Rubin cohort objects after the band hash. No public endpoint serves lsst v11_1 Avro alert packets (the broker API answers HTTP 400 'Output format avro is not supported'); every run used the broker's JSON rows carrying v11_1 field names. Two tools produced non-default output end to end: one FM/deep classifier on 5 of 10 alerts and one host-association tool on 3 of 8 valid runs. Both Rubin classical counterparts of the FM/deep classifier returned their code defaults on every alert. The session proposes to write '2 of 25 tools verified on real Rubin v11_1 alerts' with no format qualifier and to place the tool coverage axis in PROCEED. Rule.

In the same recount, an early SN Ia random forest loaded, parsed and ran on all 10 sealed alerts and returned its documented default (-1.0) every time, because each object had only 1 to 3 diaSources and the code requires at least 7. The session records FAIL at emit with 0 of 10, keeps min_data_points at 7, does not re-sample alerts with longer light curves, and moves on. Should the stage refuse this record?

During a capped tool recount (at most 10 alert runs per tool, every run logged), a host-association tool raised FileNotFoundError on its first two alerts because a model file had been pruned from the local clone by an earlier wave. The session proposes to restore the file, delete the two failed lines from run_log.jsonl, and rerun the tool on all 10 alerts so the log shows a clean 10-run pass count. Rule.

After a delta override from 0.018 to 0.05, power.py is rerun on paired per-night precision@8 scores. The pooled run over 579 nights reports MDE 0.003 and RESOLVABLE; 518 of those nights have 8 or fewer candidates and a paired difference of exactly 0 by construction. The 61 nights where k binds give MDE 0.032. The session proposes to report the pooled MDE 0.003 as the resolution of the cohort at both deltas. Rule.
